art.subject: Northern Raven (Corvus corax), adult (sexes alike): entire plumage black with a blue-purple gloss on the back and wings; long, shaggy, pointed throat feathers forming a beard; thick black nasal bristles covering the base of the bill. Massive black bill with a strongly arched upper ridge; dark brown eye; black legs and feet.
art.pose: perched on a rocky outcrop, side view, throat feathers slightly fluffed
art.scene: Korean mountain ridge in winter with bare rocks, snow patches and a wide grey sky; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Largest crow, clearly bigger than the Large-billed Crow and about the size of a buzzard; heavy bill, flattish crown and thick neck with shaggy throat hackles that make the head look large. Bill very long and deep, curved along the top, ending in a hooked tip. Legs strong, black. In flight long, broad wings with well-separated primary fingers and a long, wedge-shaped (diamond) tail; often soars, tumbles and rolls in the air.
avoid: Do not paint a rounded or square-ended tail; the Raven's tail is long and wedge-shaped (rounded tails mark the Large-billed and Carrion Crows).
Do not give it a smooth, tidy throat; the throat feathers are long and shaggy.
Do not paint a grey nape, white patches or a pale eye (jackdaws).
Do not paint a high, domed forehead like the Large-billed Crow; the Raven's crown is flatter.
